title: State-conditioned frozen expert router opportunity audit
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A router trained only on legal hand-start private-card and seat features can exploit complementary Standard10 and diverse_league5 strengths across four training opponents, retain both experts, and improve over Standard10 on three SHA-disjoint holdout opponents and independent deck seeds.
material_change: Reuse the completed three-seed PSRO raw hand evidence without generating hands. Fit two fixed ridge outcome models with leave-one-training-opponent-out alpha selection, freeze the resulting whole-hand expert gate, and evaluate it only on holdout opponents 6-8 using an unbiased independent-stream policy-value estimator and bootstrap confidence intervals.
baseline: Frozen Standard10 whole-hand policy on identical holdout opponent cohorts; diverse_league5 is the alternate expert, not a new checkpoint.
notes: Preregistered gates: exact source hashes and coverage; selected expert fraction between 5% and 95%; pooled holdout router-minus-Standard10 >5 bb/100 with 95% bootstrap lower bound >0; positive point delta on all three holdout opponents, both seats, and at least two of three deck seeds. Claim scope is offline whole-hand router feasibility only, not per-decision optimality, Slumbot strength, or newly generated environment hands.
All source gzip hashes and 3x9216 paired-row coverage were verified. Three targeted tests and the full 299-test AlphaHoldem suite passed. No new policy query or environment hand was generated.

result.summary: Reused the complete three-seed PSRO evidence to fit a legal-information whole-hand router between Standard10 and diverse_league5. The router retained both experts and had a pooled +51.54 bb/100 point estimate, but its independent-stream 95% bootstrap CI was [-121.64,+227.90], every training-CV alpha had a negative worst-opponent fold, holdout opponent8 was -43.04, and seed1 was -108.79 bb/100.
result.conclusion: Hand-start private cards and seat do not provide stable cross-opponent expert-routing signal at this evidence scale. The positive pooled point is statistically unresolved and contradicted by one holdout opponent and one deck seed. This rejects the whole-hand router opportunity, not decision-level mixture-of-experts or long-horizon learning; zero new training/evaluation hands were generated.
result.next_step: Do not train or externally test this router and do not increase the same unpaired matrix merely to rescue its point estimate. Choose a decision-level learned credit mechanism with broad on-policy state coverage, Standard10 preservation, multi-seed geometric checkpoints, and an early proxy/external alignment control before large-scale allocation.
